provenance.notAvailable: The project conversations "Refine ThermaLens Thesis", "Paper Structure Review", "Explain Translation Invariance" and "Sustainability Essay Outline" are not in this repository and could not be opened here (they are not in the connected Drive). The Master Map preserves the Paper Structure Review sequence; the Chain A questions are taken from Nadia's recollection recorded verbatim in the 2026-11-16 decisions. Nothing below is quoted from those conversations directly.
provenance.rule: Question → mathematical relation discovered → next question created by that relation. No theorem-first ordering.

master.title: What is a signal? — Make the invisible visible
master.q: What is a signal? (MM)
master.rel: "something physical can be represented by a mathematical function" (MM): x(t)
master.nxt: what if the signal measured electrical power instead of sound? (MM, #2)
master.carries: The waveform remains available for the next interactive. (MM)
master.repo: OB1; Part II (signals); Act I–IV teaching order

master.title: Music as a mathematical language — Build your own sound
master.q: what if the signal measured electrical power instead of sound? (MM)
master.rel: "A function can represent different physical phenomena, but its meaning depends on what is measured." (MM)
master.nxt: find the repeating pattern (#3); the meaning of a measured quantity returns at #11 and #20
master.carries: A function can represent different physical phenomena, but its meaning depends on what is measured. (MM)
master.repo: OB1 (shared vocabulary ≠ shared object), A3, ON9

master.title: Periodicity in nature — Find the repeating pattern
master.q: does a segment align with the rest of the signal, and what happens for a nonperiodic sound? (MM)
master.rel: a period: x(t + T) = x(t); "Repetition introduces a mathematical transformation that preserves a pattern." (MM)
master.nxt: "What remains unchanged when the pattern shifts?" (MM)
master.carries: Repetition introduces a mathematical transformation that preserves a pattern. (MM)
master.repo: R6, T1, C8, I1; Act IV; Pair B (T-PAIRB)

master.title: Symmetry across space and time — Move without changing
master.q: "What remains unchanged when the pattern shifts?" (MM)
master.rel: translation T_τ and the rotating wheel: "Symmetry is connected to what remains unchanged when something moves or transforms." (MM)
master.nxt: "Could the same pattern have another representation?" (MM)
master.carries: Symmetry is connected to what remains unchanged when something moves or transforms. (MM)
master.repo: T1–T4 (translation → correlation → symmetry defect), TA0, the rotation case of the S4 trichotomy

master.title: What is a representation? — One thing, different mathematical views
master.q: "Are these different objects, or different descriptions of one object?" (MM)
master.rel: "Mathematical representations can look different while preserving relationships." (MM)
master.nxt: Fourier: "This prepares the visitor for Fourier analysis." (MM)
master.carries: Mathematical representations can look different while preserving relationships. This prepares the visitor for Fourier analysis. (MM)
master.repo: T-REPRESENTATION, TA0 (R1 covariance), Act III

master.title: Fourier series — Construct a complex wave from circles
master.q: can a complex wave be built from rotating points? (MM)
master.rel: f = Σ c_k e^(2πikt); "Complex signals can be represented as combinations of simpler basis functions." (MM)
master.nxt: "Why can these components be separated?" (MM)
master.carries: Complex signals can be represented as combinations of simpler basis functions. (MM)
master.repo: R1, R2, R6 (the rotating point), D3

master.title: Fourier coefficients and orthonormal bases — Give every harmonic a role
master.q: "Why can these components be separated?" (MM)
master.rel: the coefficient is a projection: f̂(n) = ⟨f, e^(2πint)⟩ (CP §1b); removing a coefficient removes exactly that component; f̂(k) = 0 while f ≠ 0
master.nxt: what does that zero mean? f̂(k) = 0 "does not mean f = 0. … It means a relation between f and the mode e_k." (brief)
master.carries: Each coefficient specifies how much of a basis component contributes to the overall representation. (MM)
master.repo: R2, Z7; Master Map #7 interactive (built)

master.title: Orthogonality and zero — Find the relationship that disappears
master.q: what does a zero coefficient, or a zero dot product, mean?
master.rel: ⟨e_j, e_k⟩ = δ_jk; ⟨u, v⟩ = 0; "zero not as an empty space, but as the result of a particular mathematical relationship" (MM); projection residual ⊥ retained part; Pythagoras
master.nxt: "What does perpendicular mean beyond three dimensions?" (MM)
master.carries: Orthogonality is a property defined through an inner product, not only through visible perpendicular lines. (MM)
master.repo: ON1–ON3, Z4, Z7, BR1–BR3; #8 interactive (built)

master.title: Orthogonality beyond visible dimensions — Explore what cannot be seen
master.q: "What does perpendicular mean beyond three dimensions?" (MM)
master.rel: inner products in ℝⁿ and L²; a projection can show perpendicular vectors that are not orthogonal (O1b); "Geometry is not limited to physically visible dimensions." (MM)
master.nxt: what is reached in the limit of infinitely many components (#10); what larger geometry stands behind a visible shadow (Act III, R4 construction)
master.carries: Geometry is not limited to physically visible dimensions. (MM)
master.repo: ON4, ON5, R8, H1, H2 (R4 tetrahedral construction), T-BEYOND-3D, Act III

master.title: Mean-square convergence — Watch infinity being approached
master.q: "how an indefinitely extendable process can approach or define a bounded or finite structure" (G2 2)
master.rel: ‖S_N − f‖₂ → 0 while the pointwise overshoot persists (C8c FAIL kept, C8c2); "Convergence depends on how we define and measure closeness." (MM)
master.nxt: "Where did the magnitude go?" (MM, #11)
master.carries: Convergence depends on how we define and measure closeness. (MM)
master.repo: C8c, C8c2, T-INF-FIN

master.title: Squared coefficients, length, and energy — Where did the magnitude go?
master.q: "What does mathematical energy actually measure?" (MM); "What does squared mathematical magnitude actually mean when it is not literally physical energy?" (RD, R16)
master.rel: ‖f‖² = Σ|f̂(k)|² (Parseval, R3); squared magnitude is additive under orthogonal decomposition; "Squared magnitude can be preserved across representations, but its physical interpretation requires care." (MM)
master.nxt: "If mathematical energy is preserved, what other information distinguishes two representations?" (MM, #12)
master.carries: Squared magnitude can be preserved across representations, but its physical interpretation requires care. (MM)
master.repo: R3, ON1, ON9, A3, D26

master.title: Fourier pairs — Change the representation, not the underlying information
master.q: "If mathematical energy is preserved, what other information distinguishes two representations?" (MM)
master.rel: x(t) ↔ x̂(ω); a phase change keeps |x̂| and changes x (magnitude does not determine the signal); translation ↔ phase (R4)
master.nxt: what does zero mean in each of these structures (#13); conjugate pairs of coefficients (#17); what is lost and recovered (Act VI)
master.carries: A representation may preserve one property while expressing other properties differently. (MM)
master.repo: R4, P1, T-MAGPHASE, B5a FAIL kept, RI0, D14, D15

master.title: Zero as a mathematical cornerstone — Explore different meanings of nothing
master.q: a zero-length vector, a zero Fourier coefficient, a zero inner product, the zero-frequency component: are they the same zero? (MM)
master.rel: "Zero has different roles depending on the mathematical structure in which it appears." (MM); same visible result “0” can arise from different hidden relations (brief)
master.nxt: "the relationship between the origin, norm, squared norm, zero, and the identity matrix" (MM, #14); later the primary backbone statement and the zero questions (RD)
master.carries: Zero has different roles depending on the mathematical structure in which it appears. (MM)
master.repo: Z1–Z13, D7, D8, Act I (Chapter I), T-BACKBONE-PRIMARY

master.title: Quadratic geometry and the identity matrix — Change the rule for measuring space
master.q: What does it mean for x to be relative to zero? What is |x|, |x|²? Why does the squared norm look energy-like? What happens when M ≠ I? (brief)
master.rel: |x| = distance from x to 0; q_I(x) = x†x = |x|²; q_M(x) = x†Mx (G2 7); if x′ = Ax, x†A†MAx = x†Mx for all x ⟺ A†MA = M (CF1); "Geometry depends partly on how we define measurement." (MM)
master.nxt: which transformations keep a relation, and what do they generate (CF4; later T-GEN-DYN-Q); what distance means on a model / prediction manifold (#15)
master.carries: Geometry depends partly on how we define measurement. (MM)
master.repo: CF1–CF4, D5, D27; Gate 2 answer 7

master.title: Information geometry — Turn predictions into geometry
master.q: "What does distance mean when the valid representations lie on a model/prediction manifold?" (brief)
master.rel: ds² = dθᵀg(θ)dθ, g = JᵀJ/σ² — a position-dependent measuring rule ("distance in units of noise", CP §2); geodesics; stiff / sloppy directions; exact null directions (Z9)
master.nxt: "What exists beyond the visible model?" (MM, #16); "Could a similar geometric representation help describe time?" (MM → #18); c → ∞ as a model-family limit (G2 3 → #19)
master.carries: A family of predictions can possess a geometry, and distances in that geometry can express meaningful differences between model outputs. (MM)

master.title: Higher-dimensional prediction space — What exists beyond the visible model?
master.q: "Could a mathematical description contain relationships that cannot be represented directly in our familiar three spatial dimensions?" (MM)
master.rel: "A mathematical space can contain more structure than a single visible projection reveals." (MM); larger possibility space → rules constrain an allowable manifold → manifestation (T-MM-STORY)
master.nxt: "Could a similar geometric representation help describe time?" (MM → #18); what survives a reduction (H6, RI0)
master.carries: A mathematical space can contain more structure than a single visible projection reveals. (MM)
master.repo: MM0–MM11, D32, D33, RI0, D16, D22, T-BEYOND-3D

master.title: Conjugacy and physical pairs — Search for hidden relationships
master.q: "Do observable physical pairings or complementarities reflect deeper symmetry analogous to mathematical conjugacy?" (RD)
master.rel: for a real signal f̂(−k) = conj f̂(k) (P1) — a relation created at #7/#12, not at #16
master.nxt: mass-like and wave-like descriptions (R4, R18; MW1) — the parked mass-wave branch
master.carries: Mathematical symmetry and conjugacy provide a foundation for asking whether observed relationships point toward deeper structures. (MM)

master.title: Infinity, circular geometry, and time — Your central conjecture laboratory
master.q: "The question I want to investigate is whether this type of relationship—an unbounded quantity expressed through a bounded geometry—has deeper mathematical analogues elsewhere." (G2 8); "whether time could be bound to finite geometry and paired with another infinite structure" (MM)
master.rel: t ↦ e^(iωt): bounded, no limit, periodic; ℝ/ker χ_ω ≅ S¹; a multi-frequency torus may be dense and never periodic; the cylinder has a periodic projection and an unbounded state (Act VIII); old wording "converge to infinity" FAIL
master.nxt: "Do these relationships tell us something about nature, or only about our mathematical descriptions of it?" (MM → #19); for ★: what transformations and generators produce the continuation (T-GEN-DYN-Q)
master.carries: The visitor has enough mathematical knowledge to distinguish different forms of infinity and investigate whether a geometric relationship supports your conjecture. (MM)
master.repo: R6, I1–I3, D11, D37, D38; Act VIII record

master.title: Einstein, relativity, and mathematical reality — Change the observer
master.q: which measurements depend on the observer and which relationships remain invariant (MM); "If mathematics has boundaries imposed by the way it represents nature, can those boundaries be expanded?" (MM); c → ∞ "as a parameter limit in a family of theories/models" (G2 3)
master.rel: ΛᵀηΛ = η (L1); the boost parameter is the rapidity, tanh φ = v/c (L2); c's three roles; c → ∞: degenerate limit and Galilean contraction (L3, A8M, A8L)
master.nxt: "Can these mathematical ideas improve how we model finite physical resources?" (MM → #20); the two roles of c (H3-1, open)
master.carries: We now understand mathematical representations well enough to ask whether they preserve everything about the natural phenomena they describe. (MM)
master.repo: L1–L4, D10, D39, MM5, T-C-ROLES
